newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA supporters, opponents clash in Spain.
newsitem.headline: ETA supporters, opponents clash in Spain.

text.p: Clashes broke out in Spain's Basque region on Monday when opponents of the guerrilla organisation ETA attacked separatist supporters in anger at the rebels' killing of a young politician earlier this month.

Witnesses said the violence erupted during a march in San Sebastian by about 200 supporters of the separatist group who blamed the government for the suicide of an ETA prisoner found hanged in his cell late on Sunday.
Dozens of anti-ETA demonstrators shouting "assasins!" punched and threw rocks at some of the hundreds of sympathisers participating in the illegal march.
Police forcibly separated the two sides and broke up the march.
No casualties were reported in the scuffles.
Warders at a prison in central Spain had found ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) inmate Juan Carlos Hernando hanged with his hands loosely bound in front of him.
ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna blamed his death on the government's refusal to bring ETA inmates scattered around the country to Basque prisons.

"Once again the body of a Basque political prisoner has been found lifeless in his own cell," Herri Batasuna said in a statement. "It was the prison policy of the government that killed Juan Carlos Hernando."

Tensions have been running high in the Basque country since ETA kidnapped and killed town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco after the government refused the group's demand to transfer about 500 ETA inmates to Basque prisons.

The killing sparked national outrage and millions of Spaniards took to the streets to voice their anger. While most protests have been peaceful some turned violent when ETA opponents and sympathisers clashed.
The regional government banned a demonstration called last weekend in support of ETA. Herri Batasuna respected the order, but has appealed and is calling for a demonstration next Sunday.
